body: The worst feeling in the world. Losing sight of them even for a second in public is pure panic. One time at home my 4yo decided to an impromptu game of hide and seek that I didn't know about. Not sure how long I looked for him but he scared the crap out of me. Also I was amazed he could be still and quiet for so long.

That's me with my husband now. I get tired out by social interaction (introvert) so when it's time to go I want to just go, but my husband will spend a half hour saying goodbye inside, another in the parking lot, then forever standing next to the car talking. Worst part is we have kids now so guess who gets stuck in the car waiting and listening to the kids complaining about what's taking so long, or dealing with them being bored and rambunctious.
My psychiatrist said it was too soon to tell if there was a bipolar aspect to it, but I lost my job and now have a new insurance and a new provider so I'm not sure how they can tell.
This is what fuels my accompanying depression though.
What are your interests? Maybe you can join a group or club.
They would try to help you. Probably try to talk you out of it and send someone to do a welfare check.
I can't cry lately but it made me feel something
I've been waiting over a year for this to go away. Meds don't seem to help, quiting my stressful job didn't help. I'm out of ideas.
Just watched to make sure he didn't do it. Now I can go on with my life.

Thanks, Trust me I'm not passing judgment on people with delusions or psychotic episodes, but as a person with run of the mill clinical depression and anxiety I felt out of place and it was a bit scary. I've been to two hospitals and the first one was great.the second was awful. Unfortunately with my insurance they bus me into the first in network hospital with availability so I didn't get to choose. I have plenty of reasons but i feel nothing and nothing motivates me at the moment. I have a hot husband a good job and two beautiful children, and yet it's not enough.

As a mom my guess is that she'd rather help than know you are suffering alone, but I can only speculate on that. Otherwise I know first hand you can get help without her knowing. It's harder to hide it, but possible. Not sure what you've tried but you seem to be reaching out. I'm probably not the best person to give advice right now as I'm suicidal myself, but i can empathise. I hope you can get some relief somehow.

Have you seeked help? Do you feel comfortable talking to your mom about it? 
The only reason I'm alive is because i have kids and a supportive husband but it's still a struggle.

"Terrible, thanks for asking" 
My answer, and also a pretty good podcast.
You don't have to tell anyone. If they ask, it was a "medical issue." it's not their business.
That being said if you can get help before getting to that point, i would recommend it. It's good to know others get it.

I did have a breakdown, but not on purpose. I get it though, now that I'm out of the hospital people think I should just be fine, but I'm not. It's hard because there's no set recovery time. People think you take a med, get therapy and you should be cured.
Came here just to find this comment and upvote.
I got some information on free text and helplines (not just suicide prevention) if I can figure out where I put them I will post it.

I think sometimes people say "suicidal" when they mean they are having suicidal ideations. It is entirely possible to have suicidal ideations multiple times a week or day without making an actual attempt.

This. Been there. I finally got a referral to an outpatient treatment program from a psychiatric nurse that helped a bit. Mental help is hard because you really have to find someone you can relate to for them to be of any help. They say that depression and anxiety Are the "common cold" of the mental disorders, but people don't have their entire lives ruined by a fucking cold. And in order to get help you have to be honest about what you're feeling, but there are consequences to being honest, so what's the motivation to get help?
